title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with new contracts, funding rounds, and a few hiccups in hypersonic testing. As the U.S. government increases its budget for space resilience, private players are scrambling to secure their foothold in the ever-competitive landscape.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy in Space Tech
themes.body: Star Catcher’s recent $65 million raise and True Anomaly’s $190 million Series C highlight the growing investor appetite for space infrastructure. As the industry matures, expect more capital flowing into innovative solutions that promise to reshape our orbital landscape.

themes.title: Government Contracts Galore
themes.body: The Space Force's $4 million award to TrustPoint for LEO navigation is just one of many recent contracts aimed at enhancing U.S. capabilities in space. With the FY27 budget adding $1.4 billion for space resilience, government spending is set to fuel further advancements.

themes.title: Laser Communications Take Center Stage
themes.body: Transcelestial's testing of space-to-ground laser communications technologies could redefine data transmission in space. As bandwidth demands grow, this technology may provide the necessary boost to keep pace with increasing satellite deployments.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hiccups Persist
themes.body: The latest hypersonic glide-vehicle test slipping for the third consecutive quarter raises questions about the pace of U.S. advancements in this critical area. While the stakes are high, the delays suggest that the road to hypersonic capability is still fraught with challenges.
